clue.text: Star bringing forward a savoury food

indicators.note: bringing forward tells us to shift the named letter a from the back of the star's name to its front

parts.note: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef promotes a savoury dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing forward' moves the final A of SPICA to the front, giving A + SPIC. The word 'a' in the clue names the letter that moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Dramatist rewriting a slender work

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters of the following words are put down again in a new order

explanation.surface: A playwright revises a thin piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' rearranges the twelve letters of A SLENDER WORK into the dramatist's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Wesker was a British playwright, author of Chips with Everything and The Kitchen.

clue.text: Civilised behaviour from coppers arresting tragic woman caught out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for caught is taken away from the whole
arresting, as police hold a suspect, means the police word holds the woman's name within it

parts.note: coppers is slang for police officers
Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's tragic heroine
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Police show good manners while detaining a woman, though the catch goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' is the container signal, apt for police; 'out' then removes the cricket letter for caught from the combined word.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse is formal politeness or courtesy, a French borrowing for refined manners.

clue.text: Old Bill repeatedly climbing tree

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, means the whole run is read upwards, that is backwards
repeatedly means the bill's letters are written down twice in a row

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A police officer keeps shinning up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police, but here it splits into O and AC (bill); 'repeatedly' doubles AC to ACAC, and 'climbing' turns OACAC upwards to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: This writer with a daughter certain to be imprisoned and restrained

parts.note: this writer is the setter referring to himself, ME

indicators.note: to be imprisoned means the word for certain is locked inside A and D

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: A writer and his daughter face a sure jail sentence and keep calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be imprisoned' is the container signal: the word for certain sits between A and the daughter's letter; 'with' only joins the setter to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured speech or action is careful and controlled, a synonym of restrained.

clue.text: Tiny adult enthralling home on island

indicators.note: enthralling, holding captive, means the adult word holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: an adult is mature
in means at home

explanation.surface: A small grown-up is captivated by a home on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' is the container signal, holding home and island inside the adult word just after its first letter; 'on' only links the two inner pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniature as an adjective means very small, on a reduced scale.

clue.text: Be indecisive losing head and swear

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to waver is to be indecisive

explanation.surface: Someone dithers, then loses their cool and curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes the W from WAVER. 'swear' looks like cursing but means declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare solemnly, as one does when swearing to something.

clue.text: Like one who has sworn, spreading hate round

indicators.note: spreading means the letters of the following words are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A person takes an oath while hatred spreads around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' is the anagram signal; the definition is a phrase describing a sworn witness, so it fits the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness under oath has sworn to tell the truth, so the phrase describes one who has sworn.

clue.text: English king looking angry sinned

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
someone looking angry is red in the face

explanation.surface: An English monarch flushed with rage did wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake or do wrong, so having erred is having sinned.

clue.text: Need one control improper claim of defendant?

indicators.note: improper means the letters of the following words are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A defendant needs to keep a grip on an unsuitable claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improper' rearranges the fourteen letters of NEED ONE CONTROL into the Latin legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Nolo contendere, Latin for I do not wish to contend, is a plea by which a defendant accepts conviction without admitting guilt.

clue.text: Guitarist losing his temper in a minor car accident?

definitions.text: Guitarist losing his temper in a minor car accident?

parts.words: Guitarist losing his temper in a minor car accident?
parts.note: a Fender is a famous make of electric guitar, and a guitarist who bends notes on one could be called its bender; the whole phrase is also US slang for a small car crash in which a wing gets dented

explanation.surface: A rock musician flies into a rage after a minor bump in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful first reading pictures a Fender-playing guitarist going off the rails; the real sense is the American term for a minor collision.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is the American word for a car's wing, so bending one describes a slight collision.

clue.text: Tit flying by yellow area between lakes in coastal region

indicators.note: between means the other pieces sit inside the pair of lake letters

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, so lakes gives two Ls

indicators.note: flying means the bird's letters are sent off in a new order

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A small bird flies past a yellow patch between lakes near the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' scrambles the bird; heraldry supplies yellow; 'between' puts it all inside the pair of lake letters. 'by' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A littoral is the region of land lying along a shore or coast.

clue.text: Female coming to mountain top — it's cold

parts.note: a ridge is the long crest along a mountain's top

explanation.surface: A woman reaches a summit and finds it freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' simply joins the pieces. The definition is playful: the answer is something that is cold inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator is the kitchen appliance kept cold to chill food.

clue.text: Like Ed in Mondeo, travelling from London to Bristol?

definitions.meaning: the letters E and D do appear in Mondeo, but only read right to left, the direction of west on a map, so they are fixed in that direction
Bristol lies due west of London, so a train between them heads in that direction

explanation.surface: A man called Ed drives his Ford Mondeo from London to Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: Mondeo is a Ford family car. Read backwards, MONDEO gives OEDNOM, which contains ED; leftward on a map is west.
explanation.definitionFit: Westbound describes travel or reading heading west; ED is found in MONDEO only read right to left, which is westward on a map.

clue.text: Like soldiers en masse subjected to ridicule

definitions.meaning: soldiers housed together in a barracks block are quartered there
to jeer and heckle a speaker or player is to give them a hard time from the crowd

explanation.definitionFit: Barracked can mean lodged in barracks, as troops are, or jeered at by a crowd.

clue.text: She drives carelessly — we may be in a whirl

definitions.text: we may be in a whirl

indicators.note: carelessly means the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman drives recklessly and leaves the passengers spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' rearranges SHE DRIVES. The definition speaks as the Sufi dancers themselves, hence 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirling dervishes are Sufi Muslims who spin in religious dance, so they may be found in a whirl.

clue.text: It's not every hospital unit that gets prize

parts.note: not every hospital unit, just a single one, gives the article a
a ward is a unit of a hospital

explanation.surface: Only some hospital departments win a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says only some wards are honoured, but 'not every' just means one: A.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of achievement.

clue.text: Argue — that's what Petruchio tried to do, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is to be taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.words: that's what Petruchio tried to do
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Taming of the Shrew, Petruchio sets out to change the nature of his bride Katherina, known as Kate

explanation.surface: To argue is what Shakespeare's Petruchio spent a play trying to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says the answer sounds like 'alter Kate', what Petruchio tries to do to his bride in The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to argue or quarrel heatedly, as Petruchio and Kate famously do.

clue.text: Complete quiet, always poetic

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Total silence has always been poetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means utter or absolute, as in sheer nonsense, so it is a synonym of complete.

clue.text: Fungus that's rare, unusual

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of the two words are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a mushroom is a rare find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges THATS RARE; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthstar is a fungus whose outer skin splits into a star shape around a central puffball.

clue.text: Innocent rapture? There's hidden catch

indicators.note: hidden says the answer lies within the run of letters in the two words before it

explanation.surface: A naive bliss conceals a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through innocENT RAPture.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch, as in a snare or by trickery.

clue.text: Writer leaving a university, a female

indicators.note: leaving means the letters for a and university depart from the writer word

parts.note: an author is a writer

explanation.surface: An author quits a university, and so does a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes A and U from AUTHOR, leaving THOR, and the second 'a' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a woman's name, so in crossword terms it can stand for a female.

clue.text: Hymn fades with one listener falling over

parts.note: to fade away is to die
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: falling over means the listener's letters are toppled and read backwards

parts.note: an ear is a listener

explanation.surface: A hymn trails off as a member of the congregation keels over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling over' reverses EAR to RAE; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies Irae, the day of wrath, is a medieval Latin hymn sung in the Requiem Mass.

clue.text: Series of notes left in seat

indicators.note: in means the letter for left is placed inside the seat

parts.note: a sofa is a seat

explanation.surface: Some memos have been abandoned on a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series of notes' suggests memos, but means the musical scale do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol-fa is the system of naming the notes of the scale do, re, mi, fa, sol and so on.

clue.text: Foremost character in baseball, famous American?

definitions.text: Foremost character in baseball, famous American?

indicators.note: foremost character in means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president, is a famous American

explanation.surface: A question about the leading figure in American baseball.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth, the legendary New York Yankees slugger, is the foremost character in baseball; the wordplay takes B and adds ABE (Lincoln).
explanation.definitionFit: Babe Ruth was baseball's most celebrated player and a famous American.

clue.text: Wicked knave breaking into two houses and hiding fifty pounds in cape

indicators.note: hiding means the letters for fifty and pounds are concealed inside
breaking into means the mixed-up letters burst in between the two house abbreviations

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house, so two houses gives HO twice
HO is the abbreviation for house, so two houses gives HO twice

indicators.note: wicked means the letters of the rogue are mixed up

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A villain burgles two homes and stashes fifty pounds in a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' scrambles the rogue, 'breaking into' sets that between two house abbreviations, and 'hiding' tucks fifty and pounds inside. The Dutch port's name means Cape of Holland, so 'cape' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoek van Holland, the Hook of Holland, is a Dutch headland and ferry port, so it is literally a cape.

clue.text: Feature of diamonds, such being studded into gear

definitions.text: Feature of diamonds, such being studded into gear

indicators.note: being studded into means the diamond letter is set inside the gear like a stud

parts.note: harness is gear or tackle for a horse
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Diamonds set into a horse's harness show off their toughness.
explanation.walkthrough: D (diamonds) goes inside HARNESS; the whole clue also describes the stones' famous property.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardness is the defining feature of diamond, the hardest natural substance.

clue.text: Said to be no more than a titular chieftain

indicators.note: said to be means the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: no more than a chieftain is a mere one

explanation.surface: Someone is described as merely a chief in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said to be' tells us the answer sounds like 'a mere'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, or emir, is a Muslim ruler or chieftain, often holding a title rather than real power.
